Postgraduate Statistics
Become an expert in collecting, analysing, and interpreting data, and boost your career options with Postgraduate Statistics.
Overview
Qualifications
People
Deep dive into theory and practical applications
Study postgraduate Statistics to gain advanced expertise in data analysis and master statistical techniques. Discover meaningful patterns in data and use your insights to guide effective decision-making.
You’ll work with inspiring academics recognised for their research and teaching. Many of them have won awards for their work.
Available qualifications
Bachelor of Science with Honours
Graduate Diploma in Science
Master of Applied Statistics
Master of Science by coursework and thesis
Master of Science by thesis
Postgraduate Certificate in Science
Postgraduate Diploma in Science
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD)
Research opportunities
There are a range of postgraduate study options that allow you to focus on research that interests you. We work with researchers in many disciplines, including:
ecology
engineering
geophysics
linguistics
music
psychology.
You’ll get a wide range of research opportunities, thanks to the School’s success in winning grants.
Explore your thesis options by viewing a list of postgraduate supervisors in Statistics and seeing their research interests.
School of Mathematics and Statistics
I love that I get to combine statistics and marine biology. It’s exciting to apply what I’ve learnt to real-world data.

Full story
️Future careers
The demand for people with statistical expertise grows as more data is collected and needs to be analysed. Employers want to use this data to inform better decision-making.
Fields you can work in
There are work opportunities in research, analysis, policy, and management.
You could work in:
sciences, such as biology or medicine
education
engineering
business, finance, and economics
government.
Jobs you might do
Recent Statistics graduates have taken on roles as:
actuaries
data analysts
data scientists
risk analysts
statisticians.
Who you might work for
You might work in the public or private sector. You could join a:
data science company
research institute
medical research team
market research firm
insurance company
bank
university.
You could work across most areas of government, such as ministries for health, education, social development, or Stats New Zealand.
Scholarships
You can look for scholarships based on your level of study, subject area, and background. Search the scholarships database to find out what’s on offer and how to apply.
Browse postgraduate and doctoral scholarships
Search scholarships.
Work opportunities
Work as a tutor
The School of Mathematics and Statistics has a number of vacancies across undergraduate Mathematics, Engineering Mathematics, Statistics, and Data Science courses.
You might be able to work marking assignments or working as a tutor or teaching assistant.
Find out more about becoming a tutor
Complete the online form.
Work as a research assistant
You may be able to work as a research assistant while you study. These are fixed-term, short contracts where you assist an academic on a specific research project.
These contracts are decided in negotiation with academics in an area of interest.
Community
Postgraduate study at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington will help you build valuable relationships and networks with peers, University staff, and future colleagues.
Join a school that attracts students and staff from around the world, bringing a lively multicultural atmosphere. You’ll have opportunities to attend events, seminars, workshops, and social functions.
The Postgraduate Students’ Association can give you information on study at the University and provides a voice for you on campus.
Wellington connections
Take advantage of the University’s links with the many government departments, research institutes, and businesses based in Wellington. Staff and students are involved in research collaborations with organisations, including:
Statistics New Zealand
Department of Conservation
Wellington City Council
GNS Science
NIWA
data science companies in the private sector.
You can build your professional networks and apply your learning to real-world data. The Master of Applied Statistics offers an internship to practice these skills.
